mainTopic: Selling deposited חמץ, and רבי יהודה's two תודה loaves on the Temple colonnade: where they sat, why they were called פסולות, and how they signaled the end of eating חמץ on ערב פסח.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer. Even the חכמים agree that a deposit facing unusual loss is sold through בית דין, and this is all the more true for חמץ, which becomes worthless after פסח. The גמרא then turns to רבי יהודה's two תודה loaves, which served as a public signal on ערב פסח. רב יהודה corrects a ברייתא to say the loaves sat 'על גג האיצטבא', on the roof of the colonnade, where everyone could see them. רחבא and a ברייתא add that הר הבית had a double colonnade. Next the גמרא asks why the loaves were called פסולות. רבי חנינא says so many תודות were brought on the thirteenth that leftovers became פסול through לינה, since no תודה is brought on the fourteenth or during פסח. רבי ינאי says the loaves were really כשרות but could not be eaten. After rejecting the lost-animal case, the גמרא settles on a case where the animal was slaughtered but its blood spilled, which works according to רבי or, in a narrower case, according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Finally, a תוספתא in the name of רבי אלעזר says the loaves were fit and describes the signal: eat, wait, then burn. אבא שאול's teaching begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even the Sages agree: an unusual loss means selling through the court, and all the more so for חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The חכמים' rule against touching a deposit applies only to a normal rate of loss. If the loss is greater than normal, the guardian sells the deposit through בית דין. With חמץ, which will be completely lost, this is all the more so.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The חכמים only said not to touch the deposit when the loss is] at the normal rate of loss. But if the loss is more than the normal rate, he sells it through בית דין. All the more so here, since the חמץ will be completely lost.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that began on the previous amud. It shows that even the חכמים would agree the guardian of deposited חמץ should sell it before פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא cited a dispute about a deposit of produce that is spoiling. The חכמים say 'don't touch it,' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says 'sell it in בית דין.' This line limits the חכמים' view to ordinary, expected loss. חמץ is the extreme case: after פסח it becomes forbidden forever, so its value drops to zero.

keyTerms.meaning: the normal, expected amount of loss (e.g., from rot or mice)
he sells them under the supervision of the court
all the more so
they are completely lost

steps.whatToRemember: Even the חכמים allow selling a deposit when the loss is unusually large. Deposited חמץ before פסח is the strongest case, because it becomes totally worthless.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'בכדי חסרונן' continue a thought from the previous section about the dispute over spoiling deposits.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a guardian must protect the owner's money. When a deposit is about to be completely lost, selling it is the right way to look after it.

phrases.english: [that is only] when the loss is at the normal rate,
phrases.notes: Completes the previous line: the חכמים said 'do not touch' only in this case.

phrases.english: but if the loss is more than the normal rate —
he sells them through the court.
And all the more so here [with חמץ],
since it will be completely lost.
phrases.notes: חמץ that was owned during פסח stays forbidden forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל יותר מכדי חסרונן מוכרן בבית דין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun earlier about the חכמים' view on spoiling deposits.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the opposing view (אוקימתא of the חכמים' ruling to normal loss)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the חכמים forbid selling deposited חמץ, since they say not to touch a deposit even if it is being lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים forbid touching it only for normal loss. With excessive loss, and certainly total loss as with חמץ, even they agree it is sold through בית דין.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה on the two loaves, and a ברייתא version saying 'on the bench'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about רבי יהודה's two loaves. A reciter of ברייתות then recites, in front of רב יהודה, that the loaves were placed 'על גב האיצטבא', on the bench.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And furthermore, רבי יהודה said: two loaves, etc.' The reciter taught in front of רב יהודה: 'On the bench (על גב האיצטבא).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה and presents one wording of where the loaves were placed. This sets up רב יהודה's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says two disqualified תודה loaves were displayed in the Temple as a public signal: when one was removed, people stopped eating חמץ, and when both were removed, people burned it. The reciter's version puts them 'על גב', which suggests a low bench. That wording is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: two loaves (here, loaves of a קרבן תודה)
a reciter who memorized and recited ברייתות in the study hall
in front of him
on top of / upon
a bench, or a colonnade/portico

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה as a heading.

phrases.english: Two loaves, etc.
A reciter taught in front of Rav Yehuda:
'On the bench.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תני תנא קמיה דרב יהודה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברייתא version states the loaves were placed 'על גב האיצטבא'.

steps.title: רב יהודה objects: the loaves were not meant to be hidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה challenges the reciter's version. Why would the loaves need to be hidden away? Their whole purpose was to be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does he need to hide them away?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה attacks the wording 'על גב האיצטבא' because it puts the loaves somewhere hard to see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves were a public signal telling everyone when to stop eating חמץ. A spot on a bench would hide them among people and pillars. A signal that cannot be seen defeats its own purpose, so the wording must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: and is it so that...? (a rhetorical challenge)
to hide them away / put them out of sight

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי לְהַצְנִיעָן הוּא צָרִיךְ?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Does he need to hide them away?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי להצניען הוא צריך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording recited in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The loaves are a public signal, so a hidden location contradicts their purpose.

steps.title: Corrected wording: 'on the roof of the colonnade'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה fixes the text to 'על גג האיצטבא', on the roof of the colonnade, where everyone could see the loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach instead: 'On the roof of the colonnade (על גג האיצטבא).'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה resolves his own objection by changing a single letter in the text, from גב to גג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing ב to ג turns 'on the bench' into 'on the roof.' Now the loaves sit high up on top of the colonnade, visible to the whole crowd on הר הבית. This fits their job as a signal.

keyTerms.meaning: recite / teach it this way (a correction of wording)
on the roof of

steps.confusionAlert: גב and גג look and sound almost the same. The whole correction is a single letter, so read carefully.

phrases.english: Teach: 'On the roof of the colonnade.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תני על גג האיצטבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loaves were placed on a bench, out of sight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaves were placed on the roof of the colonnade, in full public view.

steps.title: רחבא: הר הבית had a double colonnade
steps.stepSummary: רחבא reports in the name of רבי יהודה that הר הבית was surrounded by a double colonnade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבא said in the name of רבי יהודה: הר הבית was a double colonnade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds background on the colonnade (איצטבא) just mentioned, describing what it looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the loaves sat on the colonnade's roof, the גמרא describes the structure. הר הבית was ringed by two rows of pillars, one inside the other, with a roofed walkway.

keyTerms.meaning: the Temple Mount
a colonnade, a roofed row of pillars
doubled

phrases.english: Rachava said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:
The Temple Mount was a double colonnade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רחבא אמר רבי יהודה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the structure (איצטבא) named in the corrected text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הר הבית was surrounded by a double colonnade.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the double colonnade
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same fact. רבי יהודה adds that the structure was called an 'איסטוונית', a colonnade within a colonnade.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so: הר הבית was a double colonnade. רבי יהודה says: it was called an 'איסטוונית', a colonnade inside a colonnade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רחבא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms רחבא's report word for word. It also adds the structure's name, 'איסטוונית', and spells out what 'double' means: one colonnade standing inside another.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a support)
a double colonnade (a name for the structure)
inside of

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
The Temple Mount was a double colonnade.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It was called an 'istevanit' —
a colonnade inside a colonnade.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא נמי הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רחבא's statement that הר הבית had a double colonnade
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording, plus רבי יהודה's name for it, 'איסטוונית'

steps.title: Why were the two loaves disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the word 'פסולות' from the משנה and asks what made these loaves disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Disqualified, etc.' Why were they disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה. It wants to know what caused the loaves to become פסולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the displayed loaves were disqualified but does not say why. The גמרא wants the cause, which sets up רבי חנינא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: disqualified (unfit to be eaten as a קרבן)
why?

phrases.english: 'Disqualified, etc.'
Why were they disqualified?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמאי פסולות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and asks about the next detail.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What caused the two displayed loaves to be disqualified.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: there were so many that leftovers became disqualified by לינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that so many תודה offerings were brought at this time that the כהנים could not eat all the loaves in time. The leftovers became disqualified by לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: since there were so many, they became disqualified by being left past their time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question. The loaves were simply leftovers from an overload of תודה offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן תודה must be eaten within a limited time. If it is left beyond that time, it becomes disqualified (לינה). Right before פסח there were far more loaves than could be eaten. The leftovers were unfit anyway, so they could be used as the public signal.

keyTerms.meaning: since / because
numerous
being left past the allowed time, which disqualifies a קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Since they were numerous —
they became disqualified by being left over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי חנינא מתוך שהיו מרובות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So many תודות were brought that leftover loaves were disqualified by לינה.

steps.title: Why so many: no תודה may be brought during פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains why so many תודות came right before פסח. A תודה cannot be brought during the holiday, because some of its loaves are חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: one does not bring a תודה during פסח, because of the חמץ in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי חנינא's claim that there were 'many' offerings by explaining what caused the rush.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה is brought with forty loaves, ten of them חמץ. So it cannot be offered on פסח. Everyone who owed a תודה hurried to bring it before the holiday, which created the overflow that led to leftovers.

keyTerms.meaning: a thanksgiving offering, brought with forty loaves (ten of them חמץ)
the festival of פסח
leavened bread

steps.whatToRemember: The loaves on the colonnade were leftover תודה loaves. They were disqualified by לינה because of the pre-פסח rush, since no תודה can be brought during פסח.

phrases.english: As it was taught: one does not bring a thanksgiving offering
during the festival of Passover, because of the leavened bread in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא אין מביאין תודה בחג המצות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the 'מרובות' claim of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that the תודות were numerous before פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that no תודה is brought during פסח because of its חמץ loaves

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: why did it need to explain that a תודה cannot be brought on פסח? That is obvious, because its loaves include חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the ברייתא from Step 9. Everyone already knows a תודה with חמץ loaves cannot be brought on פסח, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא should not waste words on something obvious. The objection forces us to find a less obvious point the ברייתא is really making.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Used to challenge a teaching that seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: Is it not obvious?
phrases.notes: Obvious that a תודה, which has חמץ loaves, cannot be brought on פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא quoted in Step 9 for stating something obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a תודה is not brought during פסח because of its חמץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is self-evident, since חמץ is forbidden on פסח. Therefore the ברייתא seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about the fourteenth of ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the ברייתא is really about bringing a תודה on the fourteenth. It holds that we do not bring קדשים into a situation that increases the chance they become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Here we are dealing with the fourteenth of ניסן. This תנא holds that we do not bring sacrifices into a situation of disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the objection. The new point of the ברייתא is that a תודה is not brought even on ערב פסח, the fourteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה normally may be eaten for a day and a night. On the fourteenth, however, its חמץ loaves must be finished by midday (the sixth hour), when חמץ becomes forbidden. Bringing it then would shorten its eating time and make it more likely to become פסול. This תנא holds that we do not do that, and this is the non-obvious point.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (a specific case).
He holds (this opinion).
We do not bring sacrifices into a situation that makes disqualification more likely.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not repeating the obvious ban on bringing a תודה during פסח. It teaches a stricter rule: avoid bringing it even on the fourteenth, before חמץ is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול is a general rule about how sacrifices are handled. It explains why the thirteenth was so crowded with תודות.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Here we are dealing with the fourteenth (of Nisan),
and he holds: one does not bring sacrifices
into a situation of disqualification.
phrases.notes: Their eating time would be cut short, which makes leftovers and disqualification more likely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הָכָא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא objection by moving the ברייתא's case to the fourteenth.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (אוקימתא) plus a guiding principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be stating the obvious ban on חמץ during פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that a תודה is not brought on the fourteenth either, because of אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול.

steps.title: So everyone brought תודות on the thirteenth
steps.stepSummary: Since a תודה could not be brought on the fourteenth, everyone brought theirs on the thirteenth. There were so many that the loaves became פסול through לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So everyone brought them on the thirteenth. Since there were so many, they became disqualified by being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning and connects it back to רבי חנינא's explanation in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the fourteenth ruled out, all the תודות were squeezed into the thirteenth. The כהנים could not eat all the loaves in time, so the leftovers became פסול. This explains the משנה's word 'פסולות'.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone.
Since, because of the fact that.
Become disqualified by being left overnight.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי חנינא, the loaves were truly פסול. Too many תודות were brought on the thirteenth, and the leftovers became פסול through לינה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר מַיְיתֵי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: And everyone brings them on the thirteenth,
and since they are so many,
they become disqualified by being left overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר מַיְיתֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of Step 11 and ties it back to רבי חנינא's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The loaves were called פסולות because the crowd of תודות on the thirteenth left loaves uneaten, and they became פסול through לינה.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: the loaves were actually kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי offers a different answer to the question of Step 7. The loaves were כשרות. They were called 'פסולות' only because their animal had not been slaughtered, so they could not yet be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ינאי they said: They were kosher. So why are they called disqualified? Because the animal sacrifice was not slaughtered for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different answer to 'why were the loaves called פסולות?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: תודה loaves become fully holy only once the תודה animal is slaughtered, and they cannot be eaten until the offering is completed. Without that slaughter they cannot be eaten. So 'פסולות' here means 'not usable', not truly disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid, kosher.
Why does he call them?
The animal sacrifice was slaughtered on their account.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ינאי disagrees with רבי חנינא. For רבי ינאי there is no לינה problem at all. The loaves are only 'stuck' without their animal.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yannai they said:
They were valid,
but then why does he call them disqualified?
Because the sacrifice was not slaughtered for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמְרוּ: כְּשֵׁירוֹת הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of Step 7 and offers a different answer than רבי חנינא's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why were the loaves on the roof called פסולות?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were כשרות. They were called פסולות only because no זבח had been slaughtered for them, so they could not be eaten.

steps.title: So slaughter the animal!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי: if the only problem is that the animal was not slaughtered, then just slaughter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him slaughter it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי ינאי. The problem he describes seems easy to fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loaves are only waiting for their animal, slaughtering it would make them permitted. So why call them 'פסולות'?

keyTerms.meaning: So let him slaughter!

phrases.english: So let him slaughter (it)!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִשְׁחוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ינאי's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's claim that the loaves were 'פסולות' only because no זבח was slaughtered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fix is simple: slaughter the animal, and the loaves become permitted.

steps.title: The animal was lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the animal meant for this תודה was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the sacrifice was lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that slaughtering was impossible because the animal was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no animal to slaughter, the loaves have no way to become permitted. That is why they are called 'פסולות'.

keyTerms.meaning: That it was lost.

phrases.english: Because the sacrifice was lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאָבַד הַזֶּבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by defining the case: the animal was lost.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal was available and could simply be slaughtered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal was lost, so it could not be slaughtered.

steps.title: So bring another animal!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: if the animal was lost, bring a different animal and slaughter it for these loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him bring another sacrifice and slaughter it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. A lost animal can be replaced, so why not use a new one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the animal still seems fixable. A replacement animal would make the loaves permitted, so the loaves still should not be 'פסולות'.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him bring another sacrifice.

phrases.english: So let him bring another sacrifice and slaughter it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַיְיתֵי זֶבַח אַחֵר וְנִשְׁחוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a lost animal leaves the loaves permanently unusable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A replacement animal could be slaughtered for the loaves.

steps.title: He tied these loaves to that specific animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the owner said 'this is the תודה and this is its bread'. That links the loaves to that one animal, following רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he said: 'This is the thanks-offering and this is its bread.' And this follows רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a new animal cannot be used. The owner bound the loaves to the specific animal that was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By designating the animal and the loaves together, the owner made the loaves belong to that animal. רבה's rule, quoted next, shows that a different animal cannot replace it. The גמרא is setting up the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the תודה and this is its bread. The animal and loaves are designated together.
And in line with רבה's opinion.

phrases.english: Because he said: 'This is the thanks-offering and this is its bread,'
and this follows Rabbah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: זוֹ תּוֹדָה וְזוֹ לַחְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by defining how the owner designated the offering.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case, supported by an Amora's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any new animal could be used with the loaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaves were tied to the lost animal, and following רבה no other תודה may be brought for them.

steps.title: רבה's rule: replace bread, not the תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if the תודה bread is lost, one brings new bread. If the תודה animal is lost, one does not bring a new animal for the existing bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה said: If the bread was lost, he brings other bread. If the thanks-offering was lost, he does not bring another thanks-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבה's rule to support the answer of Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule works in one direction only. Bread can be replaced for an existing animal. An animal cannot be replaced to 'rescue' existing bread. So the loaves on the roof remain unusable.

keyTerms.meaning: The bread was lost.
Another תודה animal.

phrases.english: As Rabbah said:
If the bread was lost, he brings other bread;

phrases.aramaic: אָבְדָה תּוֹדָה — אֵין מֵבִיא תּוֹדָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: if the thanks-offering was lost, he does not bring another thanks-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה: אָבַד הַלֶּחֶם מֵבִיא לֶחֶם אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for 'וכדרבה' in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a new animal cannot be brought for the loaves of a lost תודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's ruling: lost bread is replaced, but a lost תודה is not.

steps.title: The bread depends on the תודה
steps.stepSummary: The reason for רבה's rule: the bread comes because of the תודה, but the תודה does not come because of the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The bread comes on account of the thanks-offering, but the thanks-offering does not come on account of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבה's rule and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is the main part of the offering, and the bread is secondary to it. A secondary part can be replaced to serve the main part. The main part is never brought just to serve the secondary part.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
On account of, because of.

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule: the bread depends on the תודה and not the reverse, so a lost animal cannot be replaced to rescue designated bread. The next step challenges this lost-animal case, and the גמרא then replaces it with a different case.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The bread comes on account of the thanks-offering,
but the thanks-offering does not come on account of the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לֶחֶם גְּלַל תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבה's rule in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why can lost bread be replaced but not a lost תודה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bread is secondary to the תודה. The bread serves the animal, but the animal does not serve the bread.

steps.title: Why not just redeem the loaves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the loaves are only linked to a lost animal, redeem them and make them ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us redeem them and turn them into ordinary food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. If the bread is stuck without its animal, why burn it? Just redeem it so it becomes חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the animal is slaughtered, the loaves only have a money-value holiness, and that kind of holiness can be redeemed. So burning them seems unnecessary. The case from Steps 15-17 still does not explain why the loaves must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us redeem them (transfer their holiness onto money)
Ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.english: And let us redeem them and take them out to ordinary status!
phrases.notes: Redemption would solve the problem without burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיפְרְקִינְהוּ וְנַפְּקִינְהוּ לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case built in Steps 17-19 (lost animal, bread tied to it).
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the loaves must be burned because their animal was lost.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unslaughtered loaves are redeemable, so there is no reason to burn them.

steps.title: The animal was slaughtered but its blood spilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new case: the animal was slaughtered for the loaves, then the blood spilled before sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: really, the case is where the offering was slaughtered for them, and then the blood spilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the lost-animal case and gives a new one. The animal was slaughtered, but its blood spilled before it could be put on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שחיטה made the loaves fully holy, so they can no longer be redeemed. But without זריקת הדם, the offering is never completed, so the loaves can never be eaten. Since they can be neither redeemed nor eaten, they must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer)
The offering was slaughtered over them (for their sake)
The blood spilled

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the slaughter did nothing because the blood spilled. The slaughter already raised the loaves' holiness. Only the permission to eat is missing.

phrases.english: Rather: actually
where the offering was slaughtered over them
phrases.notes: This locks in the loaves' holiness.

phrases.english: and the blood spilled.
phrases.notes: So the offering can never be completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְעוֹלָם שֶׁנִּשְׁחַט עֲלֵיהֶן הַזֶּבַח וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by replacing the case with one where redemption is impossible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loaves were never slaughtered over, so they could be redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaughter happened, so redemption is blocked, and the spilled blood blocks eating, so burning is required.

steps.title: Whose view is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that slaughter alone fixes the loaves' holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants to know which opinion supports the idea that slaughter alone, without sprinkling, makes the loaves holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 21 depends on a specific assumption, that שחיטה by itself does the job. The גמרא checks whether everyone agrees, which prepares the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?

phrases.english: And according to whom?
phrases.notes: Asks for the source of the assumption in Step 21.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the answer in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that שחיטה alone fixes the holiness of the accompanying bread.

steps.title: It follows רבי: each permitting act works on its own
steps.stepSummary: The answer follows רבי, who holds that each of the two permitting acts raises holiness without the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי. For רבי said: Two things that permit an offering each raise the holiness, this one without that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this follows רבי. He holds that each of the two key acts, slaughtering and sprinkling, can raise the holiness level by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering becomes permitted through two acts: שחיטה and זריקה. רבי says each one separately raises the holiness of related items, like the bread. So slaughter alone is enough to make the loaves too holy to redeem.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה
Two things that permit (שחיטה and זריקה)
Each raises (the holiness) without the other

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the foundation for the whole answer in Step 21. Without it, slaughter alone would not block redemption.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi.
For Rabbi said:
Two things that permit —
raise (the holiness), this one without that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי: שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים הַמַּתִּירִין מַעֲלִין זֶה בְּלֹא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer follows רבי, who holds each permitting act raises holiness independently.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the שבועות lambs: the basic rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the שבועות lambs make their bread holy through slaughter. If both acts are done properly, the bread is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: The lambs of עצרת make the bread holy only through slaughter. How so? If he slaughtered them for their sake and sprinkled their blood for their sake, the bread is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for רבי's view. It starts with the simple case, where everything was done correctly and the bread becomes holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבועות, two lambs are brought together with the שתי הלחם. The ברייתא says the slaughter is what makes the bread holy. In the basic case, both acts are done with the right intention (לשמן), so the bread is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The lambs of שבועות, brought with the two loaves
For their own sake (with the correct intention)
He sprinkled their blood on the altar

phrases.english: As it was taught:
The lambs of Atzeret (Shavuot)
do not make the bread holy
except through slaughter.
How so?
If he slaughtered them for their own sake
and sprinkled their blood for their own sake —
he has made the bread holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַלֶּחֶם אֶלָּא בִּשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבי's principle in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's principle that each permitting act raises holiness on its own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the lambs and bread of שבועות.

steps.title: Proper slaughter alone makes the bread partly holy
steps.stepSummary: If both acts were wrong, the bread is not holy. If only the slaughter was right, the bread is 'holy and not holy,' according to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered them not for their sake and sprinkled their blood not for their sake, the bread is not holy. If he slaughtered them for their sake and sprinkled their blood not for their sake, the bread is holy and not holy. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the key case. When only the slaughter was done correctly, the bread becomes partly holy. This is רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Holy and not holy' means the bread is holy enough that it cannot be redeemed, but not holy enough to be eaten. This shows that a proper שחיטה alone raises the holiness. That is exactly the situation of the תודה loaves in Step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for their own sake (with the wrong intention)
Holy and not holy: cannot be redeemed, but cannot be eaten
The words of רבי

steps.confusionAlert: 'Holy and not holy' is not a contradiction. It describes a middle level: too holy to redeem, not holy enough to eat.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered them not for their own sake
and sprinkled their blood not for their own sake —
he has not made the bread holy.
If he slaughtered them for their own sake
and sprinkled their blood not for their own sake —
the bread is holy and not holy,
phrases.notes: Cannot be redeemed, cannot be eaten.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָן לִשְׁמָן וְזָרַק דָּמָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן לֶחֶם קָדוֹשׁ וְאֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives the case that actually proves רבי's principle.
steps.raayaObject: That slaughter alone fixes the bread's holiness so it cannot be redeemed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's ruling 'לחם קדוש ואינו קדוש' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: both acts are needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees and holds the bread is holy only when both slaughter and sprinkling are done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: The bread is never holy until he slaughters them for their sake and sprinkles their blood for their sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a disagreeing view. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says slaughter alone does nothing for the bread. Both acts must be done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to him, the תודה loaves in Step 21 would seem to still be redeemable, since the blood was never sprinkled. That is why the גמרא first attributed its answer to רבי. The next step shows a way his view can fit too.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי
Until he slaughters

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה loaves must be burned because the animal was slaughtered (so no redemption) but the blood spilled (so no eating). This fits רבי, who holds that שחיטה alone raises the holiness. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires both acts, but the next step shows the case can fit his view too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
The bread is never holy,
until he slaughters for their own sake
and sprinkles their blood for their own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the ברייתא, showing why the answer must follow רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread becomes holy only when both slaughter and sprinkling are done for their own sake.

steps.title: Even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון fits: the blood was caught and then spilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the explanation can work even for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The case is where the blood was caught in a cup and then spilled before it was sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. What case are we dealing with? A case where the blood was caught in a cup and then spilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 'unfit loaves' case does not have to follow only רבי. It can fit רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too, if we picture a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said the bread becomes holy only when both שחיטה and זריקה were done properly. So the גמרא narrows the case: the blood was already caught in a holy vessel and only spilled afterward. The reason this case is enough for him comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (it follows this opinion)
With what case are we dealing here? (narrowing the case)
The blood was received (caught in a holy vessel)
Cup (the vessel that catches the blood)
Spilled

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
with what case are we dealing here?
For instance, where the blood was received in a cup and then spilled.
phrases.notes: The blood was spilled after it was caught, so it was never sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 a second way. The case now fits רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון from step 26, not only רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only רבי, who says שחיטה alone makes the bread holy, could explain the 'unfit loaves' case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון can explain it, if the blood was caught in a cup and only then spilled.

steps.title: The reason: blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his father רבי שמעון. Blood that is standing ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, who said: anything standing ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why catching the blood is enough for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He uses his father's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood is in the cup, it is ready to be sprinkled. By the rule כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי, it counts as sprinkled, so the bread becomes holy. But no real זריקה happened, so the bread cannot be eaten. That is exactly why the loaves are 'unfit'.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his father (רבי שמעון)
Whatever stands ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The rule makes the bread holy. It does NOT make the bread permitted to eat. For eating, a real זריקה is still needed. That is why the loaves are holy but unfit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: 'counts as done' can work for one law (holiness) but not for another (eating).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לֵיהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds like his father,
who said: anything that stands ready to be sprinkled
is treated as if it was already sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לֵיהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the case in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supporting principle for the narrowed case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a real זריקה, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would say the bread is not holy at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood caught in a cup counts as sprinkled, so the bread is holy but cannot be eaten.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the 'unfit' loaves. רבי: שחיטה alone makes them holy. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the blood was caught and then spilled, and כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי. Either way, the loaves are holy but cannot be eaten.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the loaves were fit and served as a signal
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי אלעזר, a ברייתא says the loaves were fit. While both loaves lay there, people ate חמץ. When one was removed, people waited, neither eating nor burning. When both were removed, everyone burned their חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי אלעזר: the loaves were fit. As long as they lay there, all the people ate. When one was taken away, people waited, not eating and not burning. When both were taken away, everyone began to burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different tradition. Here the loaves were not unfit at all. It also explains how the loaves worked as a signal on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא worked hard to explain why the loaves were 'unfit'. This ברייתא simply says they were fit, so that whole problem goes away. The ברייתא also lays out three stages of the signal: eat, wait, burn.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Fit, valid
Lying in place
Hold in suspense (neither eat nor burn)
Burn (the חמץ)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the three-stage ערב פסח system: a time to eat חמץ, a time when it is forbidden but not yet burned, and a time to burn it.

phrases.english: It was taught: in the name of Rabbi Elazar they said:
The loaves were fit.
As long as they were lying there,
all the people ate (חמץ).
When one of them was taken away, they held in suspense:
they neither ate nor burned.
When both were taken away,
they all began burning (their חמץ).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמְרוּ: כְּשֵׁירוֹת הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining why the loaves were 'unfit' to a tradition that says they were fit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves were fit. Both in place: eat. One removed: wait. Both removed: burn.

steps.title: Introducing אבא שאול's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another ברייתא in the name of אבא שאול. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אבא שאול says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is opening a new ברייתא, and אבא שאול's actual words come in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening formula appears here. It tells us a new תנא is about to add another view on the ערב פסח signal. Wait for the next passage to see what he says.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A תנא whose teaching follows

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Shaul says:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a further ברייתא after the tradition in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only. אבא שאול's ruling follows on the next amud.
